source.title: Antipsychotic-like Effects of M4 Positive Allosteric Modulators Are Mediated by CB2 Receptor-Dependent Inhibition of Dopamine Release

confidence_rationale: Strong, mechanistically-resolved primary study (FSCV dopamine measurement + striatal slice physiology + M4 and CB2 knockouts + antipsychotic-predictive behaviour) directly establishing that M4 activation on striatal spiny projection neurons depresses striatal dopamine release and produces antipsychotic-like effects WITHOUT D2 blockade. This is the precise mechanism the layer's Section 3B / PHARM-017 rests on for the dopamine-selection arm. Confidence high but below 0.8 because the bridge from 'depresses striatal dopamine release' to MECH-086's 'dampens dopamine trajectory-SELECTION gain' is REE's computational interpretation, and the effect runs through a CB2/endocannabinoid intermediary the REE story does not represent.
failure_signatures: The M4-to-dopamine effect is not direct: it requires intact CB2 cannabinoid signalling as an obligatory intermediary, so any REE account that treats M4 as a direct dopamine-selection damper omits a required relay (and a place the mechanism could break in humans).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Activation of M4 muscarinic receptors on striatal spiny projection neurons produces a sustained (>30 min) depression of striatal dopamine release, measured by fast-scan cyclic voltammetry; both this sustained dopamine-release inhibition and the antipsychotic-like behavioural efficacy of M4 positive allosteric modulators require intact CB2 cannabinoid-receptor signalling.
mapping.ree_translation: The receptor layer (Section 3B) assigns to M4 the role of damping the MECH-086 dopamine trajectory-selection plane WITHOUT D2 blockade -- the reason xanomeline (PHARM-017) is antipsychotic from the muscarinic side. Foster et al. supply the direct striatal mechanism: M4 activation does reduce striatal dopamine output and does produce antipsychotic-predictive behaviour, by a route entirely separate from postsynaptic D2 antagonism. This is the cross-plane (MECH-087) point that a muscarinic action reaches the dopamine-selection plane.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two gaps. (1) 'Striatal dopamine release' is a presynaptic dopamine-availability measure; MECH-086's 'trajectory-SELECTION gain' is a computational construct about action/option selection, which the paper does not measure. (2) The effect is CB2/endocannabinoid-dependent -- an obligatory intermediary absent from the REE account; the muscarinic-to-dopamine link is therefore indirect.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; FSCV dopamine release in striatal slices + M4/CB2 knockouts + prepulse-inhibition / antipsychotic-predictive behaviour.

confidence_components.notes: Very high source quality (Neuron, multi-method, genetic controls). Mapping_fidelity good: directly grounds 'M4 dampens striatal dopamine without D2', which is the layer's core Section 3B mechanism; the residual gap is release-vs-selection-gain and the CB2 intermediary. Transfer risk moderate (mouse striatum).
